# Lisbon Food Trip at a Glance

A 3-day plan for **2 adults** in Lisbon from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-12**, designed to stay near **€180 total** while keeping meals Portuguese, vegetarian-friendly, and light on seafood. I’ve weighted the itinerary toward bakeries, tascas, markets, and classic comfort dishes.

# Day-by-Day Lisbon Food Itinerary

## Day 1 — Baixa, Alfama, and a classic pastry start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- **Breakfast:** Pastel de nata + galão at a historic bakery in Baixa; easy start, budget-friendly, and vegetarian-safe.
- **Lunch:** **Bifana** for one, **vegetable soup + omelet or cheese toast** for the vegetarian at a casual tasca near Rossio.
- **Snack:** Another **pastel de nata** stop with espresso in the afternoon.
- **Dinner:** Shared Portuguese dinner in Alfama: **grilled chicken or pork**, **caldo verde** without chouriço for the vegetarian, plus salad and potatoes.

**Estimated spend:** €55–€60 total for 2
**Why this works:** Strong local flavor without leaning on seafood, and the pastry stop is built in early.

## Day 2 — Market visit and neighborhood dining
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg

- **Breakfast:** Coffee, toast, and fresh pastries near your hotel or at a neighborhood café.
- **Lunch:** **Mercado da Ribeira / Time Out Market** visit for flexible choices: one person can go for grilled meats or regional plates, the vegetarian can pick **salads, cheese boards, soups, or vegetable dishes**.
- **Snack:** Fruit, nuts, or a small dessert from the market or a nearby bakery.
- **Dinner:** Traditional Portuguese neighborhood restaurant in Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real: **roast chicken, pork, or steak** for the omnivore; **mushroom rice, vegetable stew, or omelet** for the vegetarian.

**Estimated spend:** €60–€65 total for 2
**Why this works:** The market gives maximum flexibility for mixed diets and satisfies your market-visit requirement.

## Day 3 — Belém-style morning, relaxed final dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg

- **Breakfast:** Head to **Belém** for coffee and **pastel de nata**; this is the best pastry-focused morning of the trip.
- **Lunch:** Simple lunch in the city center: **soup, salad, and a sandwich/tosta** for the vegetarian; **frango assado** or a steak sandwich for the other traveler.
- **Snack:** A light bakery stop or gelato while walking between sights.
- **Dinner:** Farewell meal at a traditional restaurant: choose **grilled meats** and **vegetable sides**, or a **vegetarian plate** built around rice, eggs, greens, and potatoes.

**Estimated spend:** €55–€60 total for 2
**Why this works:** Keeps the final day easy, filling, and still very Portuguese.

## Food Budget Plan

| Day | Target Spend | Main Cost Driver | Budget Tip |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Day 1 | €55–€60 | Dinner | Keep lunch simple and pastries small |
| Day 2 | €60–€65 | Market meals | Share snacks and avoid drinks at every stop |
| Day 3 | €55–€60 | Dinner | Use cafés for breakfast instead of sit-down brunch |

**Trip total target:** **€170–€185**
That is close to your **€180** cap; to stay safely under, skip alcoholic drinks, share desserts, and choose lunch spots with set plates or soup + sandwich combos.

## Simple Packing List for Lisbon

- Comfortable walking shoes
- Light jacket or cardigan for evenings
- Small umbrella or packable rain shell
- Reusable water bottle
- Sunglasses and sunscreen
- Phone charger and power bank
- Small day bag or crossbody bag
- Copies of travel documents
- A little cash plus a card
- One smart-casual outfit for nicer dinners
